message.content:
Let  
\[
\theta_w(x)=T_w(x)-T_\infty = \frac{C}{x}
\]
where \(x\) is the distance down the vertical plate from the leading edge and \(y\) is normal to the plate. I will use magnitudes; signs depend on the chosen positive direction along the plate. Assume laminar, steady, constant-property natural convection in a quiescent ambient fluid.

---

## Scaling result

Write the boundary-layer fields in self-similar form as

\[
u(y,x)\sim U(x),\qquad \theta(y,x)\sim \theta_w(x),\qquad 
\eta=\frac{y}{\delta(x)}
\]

with boundary-layer thickness \(\delta(x)\) and maximum velocity \(U(x)=u_{\max}(x)\). Continuity gives the transverse velocity scale

\[
v(y,x)\sim \frac{U\delta}{x},
\]

so at the edge of the boundary layer,

\[
v_\infty(x)\sim \frac{d}{dx}\int_0^\infty u\,dy \sim U\frac{d\delta}{dx}.
\]

### Energy balance

The energy equation,

\[
u\frac{\partial \theta}{\partial x}+v\frac{\partial \theta}{\partial y}
=\alpha \frac{\partial^2\theta}{\partial y^2},
\]

gives, to leading order,

\[
U\frac{\theta_w}{x}\sim \alpha\frac{\theta_w}{\delta^2}.
\]

Hence

\[
\delta^2\sim \frac{\alpha x}{U}.
\tag{1}
\]

### Momentum/buoyancy balance

The buoyancy force per unit volume is of order

\[
g\beta \theta_w \sim g\beta \frac{C}{x}.
\]

The inertia scale is

\[
u\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}\sim \frac{U^2}{x}.
\]

Balancing buoyancy with inertia,

\[
\frac{U^2}{x}\sim g\beta\frac{C}{x},
\]

so

\[
U(x)\sim \text{constant}.
\tag{2}
\]

From (1) and (2),

\[
\delta(x)\sim x^{1/2}.
\]

---

## Variations of the requested variables

Let the proportionality constants be absorbed into the symbols.

### 1. Boundary-layer thickness

\[
\boxed{\delta(x)\propto x^{1/2}}
\]

### 2. Maximum velocity

\[
\boxed{u_{\max}(x)\propto x^0}
\]

The maximum velocity tends to a constant for large \(x\).

### 3. Local wall heat flux

The wall heat flux is

\[
q''\sim k\frac{\theta_w}{\delta}.
\]

Therefore

\[
q''(x)\sim \frac{k\,C/x}{x^{1/2}}
\]

so

\[
\boxed{q''(x)\propto x^{-3/2}}
\]

### 4. Total heat rate \(Q\)

If \(Q(x)\) is the heat rate per unit width carried by the fluid at section \(x\),

\[
Q(x)\sim \int_0^\infty u\theta\,dy \sim U\theta_w\delta
\sim \frac{1}{x}x^{1/2}
\]

so

\[
\boxed{Q(x)\propto x^{-1/2}}
\]

If instead \(Q(x)\) means the heat transferred from the leading edge to station \(x\), then since \(dQ/dx\sim q''\propto x^{-3/2}\),

\[
Q(x)\sim \int x^{-3/2}\,dx \sim -x^{-1/2}+\text{constant}.
\]

Thus the variable part also scales as

\[
\boxed{Q(x)\propto x^{-1/2}}
\]

with an additive constant set by the leading-edge or source region.

### 5. Edge transverse velocity \(v(\infty)\)

From continuity,

\[
v_\infty(x)\sim U\frac{d\delta}{dx}.
\]

With \(U\sim \text{constant}\) and \(\delta\sim x^{1/2}\),

\[
\frac{d\delta}{dx}\sim x^{-1/2},
\]

so

\[
\boxed{v_\infty(x)\propto x^{-1/2}}
\]

---

## Summary of power-law variations

\[
\boxed{
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{Variable} & \text{Dependence on }x \\ \hline
\theta_w(x) & x^{-1}\\[2mm]
q''(x) & x^{-3/2}\\[2mm]
Q(x) & x^{-1/2}\quad \text{variable part}\\[2mm]
\delta(x) & x^{1/2}\\[2mm]
u_{\max}(x) & x^0\\[2mm]
v_\infty(x) & x^{-1/2}
\end{array}
}
\]

---

## Is the circumstance physically obtainable?

The law

\[
\theta_w\propto \frac1x
\]

is singular at \(x=0\). If imposed literally on a real plate with a sharp leading edge, it requires

\[
\theta_w\to \infty,\qquad q''\to \infty,\qquad v_\infty\to \infty
\]

as \(x\to0\). Therefore it is **not physically realizable exactly at the leading edge**.

However, it can be obtained **asymptotically** for \(x\) larger than a finite length scale \(x_0\) that represents the size of a heat source, an edge radius, or some other near-field heating region. Under that condition, the \(1/x\) wall-temperature distribution can arise if the plate is heated in such a way that the local heat flux decays like

\[
q''\propto x^{-3/2}
\]

so that the total heat input is finite after the singular leading-edge region is cut off. A possible physical realization is a concentrated or finite-size heat source near the leading edge of a vertical plate in a quiescent fluid; far downstream, the boundary-layer flow would have the self-similar form \(\delta\sim x^{1/2}\) and the temperature excess would approach a \(1/x\) law.

The flow would be physically meaningful under the usual boundary-layer conditions:

- steady, two-dimensional natural convection;
- vertical plate;
- ambient fluid quiescent and unstratified;
- constant fluid properties;
- laminar flow, so that local Reynolds and Rayleigh numbers remain below the transition threshold;
- \(x\) sufficiently large compared with the size of the heating element or leading-edge region.
